feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform roles: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by useful scale indicators. It reads clearly overall, but it is too dense, somewhat repetitive, and would be stronger with sharper outcomes and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership trajectory at NACo, showing progression from coordinator to director with increasing scope and responsibility.  
- Good credibility signals through concrete scale/details: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms.  
- Positioning is strong and modern, especially around digital governance, Drupal, analytics infrastructure, multimedia, and AI-enabled search.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable impact/results beyond activity: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, production savings, adoption rates, campaign outcomes, or governance improvements. Several bullets describe responsibilities more than achievements.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” Consolidating these sections would improve structure and scannability.  
- Fix style consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s” usage could be standardized; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”; title case is inconsistent (“Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT”). No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear public-sector positioning, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets. It would be stronger with one sharper value proposition and fewer stacked capability lists.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one concise positioning statement plus one impact-oriented sentence; foreground enterprise web modernization and governance as the clearest differentiators.
- Replace “building the platforms” with stronger, more direct phrasing like “leading” or “modernizing” for seniority and clarity.
- Consider: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Combines editorial, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search expertise to improve how complex, mission-driven institutions publish, measure, and deliver digital experiences.”
- Standardize style: use “12+ years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience” consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “AI-enabled search” would be more specific.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” repeats themes already covered in the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened into broader, less repetitive capability areas with more parallel phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, category-style phrases and keep structure parallel; e.g.: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership
- Replace vague or overlapping items with sharper terms: “Workflow automation and platform integration” → “Workflow automation and systems integration”; “AI-enabled search and content experiences” → “AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Consider a more senior framing by emphasizing leadership/operations over tasks: “Multimedia production and livestream operations” → “Multimedia and livestream operations”
- If space allows, revised version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and discovery • Workflow automation and systems integration • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Public-sector and advocacy communications” repeats the header’s “public-sector communications.”
- Several items duplicate Topline Skills almost verbatim, especially governance, analytics, AI search, and multimedia.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience and Core Competencies. Tightening wording and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and separate this from core experience.
- Shorten each item to one crisp line with parallel verbs and fewer stacked descriptors.
- Replace generic phrases like “improve discovery” and “designed for continued campaign growth” with specific outcomes, audience, or scale if available.
- Standardize style: use “AI-enabled” consistently, spell out “10 x 20-foot,” and consider “bill-specific AI chat” for clarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search overlaps with the current freelance role and Core Competencies; keep this version more project-specific.
- Advocacy Video Series repeats NACo video leadership in multiple roles; emphasize format, cadence, or channel impact to avoid redundancy.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Core Competencies

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear relevance to your headline, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the footer project summaries and prior NACo web/governance bullets. Tighten around scope, seniority, and 2–3 concrete outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4 impact-led bullets; start with strong verbs: “Built,” “Led,” “Advised,” “Developed.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing teams supported, workflow time saved, search/discovery improvements.
- Example phrasing: “Led AI-enabled search initiative across retrieval design, structured content workflows, and discovery UX to improve access to complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” and the Drupal microsite/storytelling work duplicate the “Recent Projects” footer; keep this entry higher-level and let the footer hold project detail.
- Governance/analytics/workflow language also overlaps with the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize new consulting scope and current strategic ownership.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to foreground enterprise ownership and outcomes while avoiding overlap with the earlier NACo roles on newsletters, video, and day-to-day channel management.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to emphasize enterprise outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add growth, engagement, deliverability, production volume, or campaign impact if available; otherwise shorten.
- Tighten operations bullets: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio” and “Implemented analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve executive reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Newsletter and recurring video details overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on leadership, modernization, and infrastructure.
- “Governance/publishing workflows” also appears in prior NACo roles; frame here as organization-wide standards and cross-department systems.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level: operational leadership, editorial systems, and recurring advocacy programming.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Tighten bullets to 3–4 high-value points: newsletters, advocacy video series, cross-team editorial planning, publishing workflow improvements.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: newsletter audience size/open rates, video cadence/views, number of teams coordinated, publishing volume or turnaround improvements.
- Example rewrite: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders; produced a recurring advocacy video update and improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is too close to the Director role’s opening.
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and Recent Projects; keep only if you add stronger outcomes or ownership.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around senior-level leadership outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “Editorial governance & publishing operations,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “Public-sector advocacy communications,” “Audience-centered content strategy.”
- Consider a more concise rewrite: “Enterprise digital strategy • Editorial governance & publishing operations • Cross-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Audience-centered content strategy”
- If space allows elsewhere, tie one phrase to scale or complexity, e.g. “for high-volume, multi-stakeholder organizations.”
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing “messaging,” “planning,” and “leadership” styles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with NACo experience bullets; keep this section as a summary, not a repeat.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the platforms/technical strengths most relevant to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: **Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences**
- Prioritize recent, proven strengths: put **Drupal**, **CMS modernization**, **AI-enabled search**, and **API/workflow automation** first; de-emphasize older or less central platforms.
- Consider dropping **WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages** from this topline item unless they are target-role keywords; they fit better in “Technical + IT.”
- If space allows, sharpen one phrase to outcomes orientation: **CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills higher-level and save full platform inventory for Technical + IT.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies/header language; avoid repeating it verbatim too often.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics capability and decision-making value, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization” rather than pure software enumeration.
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity” + “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider stronger wording: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboards and decision support” or “Executive reporting and performance insights.”
- Optional rewrite: “Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity) • KPI framework design • Executive reporting and dashboards • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave full tool inventory to Technical + IT.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value operational leadership and event delivery rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Virtual event production workflows”
- Consider swapping “Video production and editing” for “Broadcast-quality video production” to better reflect the in-house studio leadership in the 2022–2024 role.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing broad categories with tools/processes.
- If space allows, add one stronger scope cue: “Livestream and hybrid event delivery for advocacy, conferences and recurring programming”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; use this section to get more specific, not repeat the same wording.
- “PTZ camera systems” and “Studio operations” partially overlap with “Livestream studio workflows” in Technical + IT.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should either add proficiency/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize strongest/recent platforms first: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add level/scope instead of just names: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; custom microsites), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; if “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, don’t repeat it here.
- Consider dropping the weakest/least relevant platform if experience is limited, so the list better reflects recent impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one list broader and the other more impact-oriented.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight beside enterprise CMS tools unless supported by project context elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and modern tools most aligned with recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from basic languages to applied delivery: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group tools by function for clarity: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping version numbers unless used elsewhere consistently; “HTML” and “CSS” are cleaner than “HTML5/CSS3”
- If accurate, add scope/level in a parenthetical to strengthen credibility, e.g., “API integrations (CMS, analytics, campaign tools)” or “GitHub Actions (deployment automation)”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep the stronger phrasing in one place
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere, so avoid implying GitHub Actions is your main automation differentiator unless supported by recent experience

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems**
- Group by function to improve scanability: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Teams
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show depth: **Built and managed workflows in Airtable, Power Automate and Zapier; administered project coordination in Jira/Asana/Trello**
- Consider trimming older/generic tools if space is tight; keep the strongest, most relevant platforms first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap heavily; listing all four may feel redundant unless each was used meaningfully.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platforms to include, but this item is too bare and undersells relevance to your recent leadership in email operations. It should signal enterprise-scale email/engagement capability without repeating newsletter details already covered in work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency and standardize naming: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier for scope rather than just listing tools, e.g. **Enterprise email marketing, member communications and journey automation**
- Keep it platform-focused; let work experience carry audience size, newsletter cadence, and channel leadership metrics

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “tens of thousands,” or campaign results here; those are already covered in NACo roles
- “Engagement” may overlap with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-specific

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” It should either be tightened to a pure tools list or reframed to emphasize optimization methods and reporting outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Consider renaming to: **Analytics & Optimization Tools**
- Tighten and group for clarity: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI dashboarding**
- Replace broad terms like **SEO** and **Dashboarding** with more specific skill labels such as **technical SEO / search performance analysis** and **KPI dashboarding**
- If space allows, align with recent impact by adding a qualifier elsewhere in the CV, not here, e.g. analytics stack used to support **3.5M annual page views** and leadership reporting

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping one as strategic capabilities and this one as tools only
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating descriptive claims here

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles on workflows, video, and digital operations. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete outputs or scale you can add.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten and specify scope: “Supported web, email, social, and multimedia operations; helped streamline publishing workflows and cross-channel content delivery.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: website refresh size/timeline, number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email volume, or team size.
- Example rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported web, email, social, and multimedia operations, improved publishing workflows, contributed to a major website refresh, and produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates. Provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats language used in later NACo roles; keep this version more junior/tactical.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a notable “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the innovation/research scope and keep the multimedia point concise.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground coordination and the standout launch: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives that supported NACo program development and policy priorities.”
- Tighten the digital sentence: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If you can, add scale/outcomes: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Consider splitting into 2 bullets for readability rather than one blended paragraph.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing general digital content production; later NACo roles already cover web, video, and multimedia leadership in more depth.
- Don’t repeat “weekly video” or broader digital operations themes from 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Tighten it to emphasize current, professional production tools and avoid repeating broader multimedia themes already covered elsewhere.
